# Results - Study 95 (Holiday-Cheer) on the real tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). We derive the US
market-holiday calendar **offline, from the trading index itself** - any weekday absent
from the trading dates (and not a weekend) is a day the exchange was shut, i.e. a holiday;
the trading day immediately before it is a **pre-holiday** day. We then measure the mean
return on pre-holiday days vs all other days (HAC t-stats, Wilson win-rate intervals),
run a **pre-holiday-only** book against buy-and-hold, and split the long sample
**pre/post-1990** with a block-bootstrap test of the decay. As-of **2026-06-12**; match
the fingerprints to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Adjustment | Window | Rows | Pre-holiday days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| SPY | **total-return** | 1993-01-29 -> 2026-06-12 | 8,400 | 301 | `eb1569cc9e97` |
| ^GSPC | **price-only** (no dividends) | 1950-01-03 -> 2026-06-12 | 19,233 | 702 | `0198a54a32c0` |

> `^GSPC` is **price-only** - it carries no dividends; it is used only for the long
> sample the pre/post-1990 decay story needs, and is labelled price-only everywhere it
> is quoted. `SPY` total-return is the fair tape for the tradability question.

## The effect - pre-holiday vs every other day

| Tape | Pre-holiday mean | Other-day mean | Ratio | Gap | HAC *t* (gap) | Win-rate pre | Win-rate rest |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **^GSPC price-only (1950+)** | **18.89 bps** | 3.09 bps | **6.1x** | +15.80 bps | **+5.05** | 64.2% [60.6, 67.7] | 52.7% [52.0, 53.5] |
| SPY total-return (1993+) | 9.60 bps | 4.58 bps | 2.1x | +5.02 bps | +0.98 | 57.1% [51.5, 62.6] | 54.0% [52.9, 55.1] |

The pre-holiday day really is special in the long sample - **6x** the average day, win
rate 64% vs 53% (non-overlapping Wilson intervals), HAC *t* = **5.05**. On the modern
total-return SPY tape alone the gap is half as big and **doesn't clear the bar** (*t* =
0.98).

## The decay - pre/post-1990 (^GSPC price-only, the only tape long enough)

| Sub-period | Pre-holiday gap | HAC *t* (pre) | Pre-holiday days |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **pre-1990** | **25.13 bps** | **+7.25** | 377 |
| **post-1990** | **5.02 bps** | +1.96 | 325 |

Block-bootstrap test of the *difference* (early gap minus late gap, 20-day circular
blocks, 2000 resamples): **decay = 20.11 bps**, **P(decay > 0) = 0.999**, 95% CI **[6.78,
32.76] bps**. The effect was huge and unambiguous before Ariel (1990) published it, and
**roughly a fifth of its old size, no longer past the *t* = 2 bar**, afterwards. This is
the textbook "anomaly that faded after it was documented."

## Could you trade it? - a pre-holiday-only book (net of 1 bp/leg)

| Arm | CAGR | Sharpe (whole tape) | Sharpe (per invested day) | Days invested |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Pre-holiday-only (^GSPC PO)** | **1.54%** | 0.629 | **3.571** | 702 (3.6% of tape) |
| Buy & hold (^GSPC PO) | 8.32% | 0.587 | - | 100% |
| Pre-holiday-only (SPY TR) | 0.65% | 0.240 | 1.437 | 301 (3.6%) |
| Buy & hold (SPY TR) | 10.82% | 0.646 | - | 100% |

The pre-holiday *day itself* is a brilliant bet (per-invested-day Sharpe **3.57**) - but
there are only **~9 of them a year**. A book that sits in cash the other 96% of the time
compounds to **1.54%/yr vs 8.32%** for simply holding the index: it captures far too few
days to matter as a standalone strategy, and the modern (post-1990) version of the day is
no longer reliably positive.

## How to read it

- **Signal -> MIXED.** *Real on the long tape* (HAC *t* = 5.05, 6x the normal day,
  pre-1990 *t* = 7.25) but *weak on the modern era* (post-1990 *t* = 1.96, SPY-only *t* =
  0.98). The decay is itself highly significant (P = 0.999). Real, then faded - exactly as
  the literature reports.
- **Tradability -> MIRAGE.** The day is wonderful but rare (3.6% of the tape); a
  pre-holiday-only book earns **~1.5%/yr vs 8.3%** for buy-and-hold. There is no way to
  scale ~9 days a year into a competitive return, and the modern day no longer pays.
- **Faded since 1990? -> CONFIRMED.** The pre/post break is the canonical 1990 publication
  date, and the bootstrap puts the decay at 20 bps with P(decay>0) = 0.999.

## Reproduce

```bash
python examples/verify.py              # real tapes (this doc)
python examples/run_synthetic_demo.py  # offline positive/negative control
```
